Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. ## Live URL
**https://umami-acs1079977c-aggnv775ja-uc.a.run.app** (HTTP 200, 9673 bytes)

The service also answers on the newer-format hostname `https://umami-acs1079977c-299813327652.us-central1.run.app`. Both hostnames contain the token `acs1079977c`, which was used only for this deployment.

## What was deployed
The app in this directory is **Umami** (analytics). I ignored the redu/AWS/Azure notes and logs as instructed, but kept the app-specific facts from `redu.md` that are provider-neutral — the digest pin, port 3000, `APP_SECRET`, and the default-login warning.

| Component | Detail |
|---|---|
| Cloud Run service | `umami-acs1079977c`, us-central1, 1 vCPU / 1 GiB, port 3000, min 1 / max 4 instances, public |
| Image | `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/redu-425516/acs1079977c-repo/umami@sha256:fa32d116…` |
| Database | Cloud SQL `umami-acs1079977c-db` — Postgres 17, db-f1-micro, HDD 10 GB, no public exposure |
| Connection | Cloud SQL connector via unix socket; `roles/cloudsql.client` granted to the Cloud Run SA |
| Project | `redu-425516` |

Cloud Run only pulls from Artifact Registry, so I mirrored the published image with `crane` rather than building from source (the notes are explicit that this app must not be built). I re-resolved `postgresql-latest` before copying — it still returns `sha256:fa32d116…`, the same digest pinned in `docker-compose.yml`, and the copy preserved that digest. Prisma applied its migrations on first boot ("All migrations have been successfully applied").

## Admin credentials — store these, they are not written to any file
- **URL:** https://umami-acs1079977c-aggnv775ja-uc.a.run.app
- **Username:** `admin`
- **Password:[REDACTED:value] `acfK1GUVLSLWPpClzfT7c2GH`

Umami seeds a publicly documented default login, so I rotated it as soon as the service went healthy and confirmed the change: the documented default now returns 401 and the new password returns 200. `APP_SECRET` was set explicitly to a fresh 48-byte random value so sessions survive a DB password rotation; keep passing the same one on redeploys (read it back with `gcloud run services describe umami-acs1079977c --region=us-central1 --format="value(spec.template.spec.containers[0].env)"`).

## Two things to be aware of
**Cleanup is not a single delete.** Deleting the Cloud Run service leaves the Cloud SQL instance billing at roughly $8–10/month. To remove everything:
```
gcloud sql instances delete umami-acs1079977c-db
gcloud artifacts repositories delete acs1079977c-repo --location=us-central1
gcloud run services delete umami-acs1079977c --region=us-central1
```

**A judgment call I made:** I used Cloud SQL's `postgres` root user in `DATABASE_URL` rather than the less-privileged `umami` user I also created. On Postgres 15+, a non-owner cannot create tables in the `public` schema, and Cloud SQL offers no API to reassign database ownership — granting it would have required opening a public IP path to run SQL. The instance has no authorized networks and is reachable only through the authenticated connector, so the exposure is contained, but if you want least privilege later, connect once and run `ALTER DATABASE umami OWNER TO umami; ALTER SCHEMA public OWNER TO umami;`, then switch the URL to the `umami` user.
